title: Wonderland — Validation-Stage Funding Pitch
audience: Validation-stage funders (grant bodies, impact investors, pilot partners)

slides.title: Wonderland
slides.headline: A creative-thinking companion where the child stays the author — seeking funding to validate it
body: No outcome data yet — that is what we are raising for
slides.speaker_notes: In the next five minutes: the problem, what exists today, a 45-second demo, and exactly what we need to find out whether it works.

slides.title: Ideas die at the first answer
slides.headline: "That can't work" is often the first thing a child's idea hears
body: Creative thinking is now assessed internationally (OECD PISA 2022)
A pretty AI-made drawing is not evidence a child learned anything
Hypothesis (untested): families want tools that ask rather than answer
slides.speaker_notes: Adults, with the best intentions, answer children's ideas too fast. Creative thinking — generating, evaluating and improving ideas — is now on the international education agenda. And a beautiful drawing made mostly by AI tells us nothing about what the child learned. Our hypothesis — not yet tested — is that families want tools that ask rather than answer. I started Wonderland because I want to leave the next generation better equipped than we were.

slides.title: What exists today
slides.headline: A voice-to-drawing demonstrator built on one rule: the child decides every change
body: Exists: child speaks → drawing appears → child revises
Designed: guide asks questions instead of generating
Not yet: users, outcome data, market sizing
slides.speaker_notes: Today there is a demonstrator: a child says what they imagine, sees it drawn, and changes it step by step. The design rule is that the guide asks rather than generates. To be direct: we have no users, no outcome data and no market sizing yet. Those are what this round should produce.

slides.title: 45 seconds of the demonstrator
slides.headline: Watch who makes each decision
body: "Draw a car" → "Add a dog" → "Make the dog smaller"
slides.visual: Recorded 45 s clip with captions marking each child decision
slides.speaker_notes: [Play clip.] Each change you see was the child's call. Next comes age-adapted interaction — short voice turns for six-year-olds, more control for ten-year-olds.

slides.title: The ask: fund the validation ladder
slides.headline: [AMOUNT — to be decided by presenter] to reach two milestones
body: M1: usability study with adult testers
M2: small parent-consented pilot with independent raters
Risk: the guide may not improve child-initiated ideas — M2 is designed to find out
If not funded: continue with low-cost parent–child workshops first
slides.speaker_notes: We are not asking you to believe it works. We are asking you to fund finding out: first a usability study with adults, then a small, parent-consented pilot measuring how many ideas and changes come from the child rather than the tool, rated by independent people. If it does not help, we change it or stop. Without funding, the work continues more slowly through workshops. It is not therapy, and every study needs consent.

slides.title: Partner with us on the first pilot
slides.headline: One decision today: a conversation about M1–M2
body: Longer term: drawing and shape input, 3D, shared worlds — only if M2 says yes
slides.speaker_notes: Longer-term ideas like 3D and shared worlds only matter if the pilot says yes. The decision I'm asking for today is small: a follow-up conversation about funding M1 and M2.
